speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: For example, with our limited resources, it is going to be difficult to respond to all incidents within the same response time.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: The Home Team needs to be data-driven, tiered and differentiated in its frontline response.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: This means employing data analytics to anticipate ahead of time where safety and security emergencies might arise and intelligently deploy our resources to focus on those hotspots.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: More resources into higher priority areas for a faster response time and inevitable trade-offs will then have to be made.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Page: 69 Coming back to the Police and counter-terrorism, I want to make another point.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Despite the significant manpower challenges, we are working on considerably enhancing the size of our Emergency Response Teams (ERTs).

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: If we do not, then, in my view, we take unacceptable risks.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: This programme, which we will call PolCam 2.0, will build on the ongoing PolCam 1.0 programme which installed video cameras at all HDB blocks and multi-storey carparks.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: They are a key plank in our counter-terrorism strategy and crime-fighting strategies.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Another area where technology can help us is at our checkpoints.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Motorcyclists entering Singapore will have their passports verified by a machine and have their thumbprint scanned for identity authentication.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: This is similar to the automated lanes available for Singaporeans at passenger checkpoints.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: More efficient, more convenient, without compromising on security.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: They will allow us to do more with a limited number of officers and free up our manpower resources to be re-deployed to more critical duties.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: But technology and systems are not effective without good officers.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Mr Desmond Choo and Mr Louis Ng highlighted the importance of attracting Home Team officers and optimising our manpower resources to meet increasing demands.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Police will also enhance its scheme of service to attract young people to join the Force and to retain the good officers we already have.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: There will be a unified single scheme and a single rank structure for all Police officers.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: And good Diploma holders who join the Force can look forward to seamless advancement opportunities up the ranks.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Second, Police will introduce expert tracks to build deep specialty in the key domains of investigations, intelligence and special operations.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: There will, therefore, be new career developmental pathways for officers with specialised skills.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: These measures will help enhance the operational capability and preparedness of SPF.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Details will be announced at the Police Workplan Seminar later this month.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: We will also progressively extend the changes to the rest of the Home Team departments.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Another group of officers who play a vital role in the Home Team is our National Servicemen.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Mr Melvin Yong had observed that the number of full-time Home Team NS officers will decrease 	Page: 70 over time.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Thus, SPF and SCDF have embarked on and completed their NS transformation reviews.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: We are restructuring our plans for full-time NS officers and reservists to focus their deployment on operational roles that will have a direct impact on ground situations and give them more opportunities to assume leadership and specialist roles.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Beyond the Home Team, Auxiliary Police forces are important partners.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: I think Ms Sylvia Lim spoke about APOs.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: APOs are deployed for a range of functions, including protecting sensitive installations and supporting Police deployment at major events.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: They are used as a complement of Police resources.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: They are either Singapore Citizens, PRs who are Malaysian citizens, or Malaysian citizens.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Ms Lim asked if there is a ratio of five Malaysians to one Singaporean.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: More than half of the APOs are Singaporeans and that is not by chance.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: My Ministry has deliberately required that there be a Singaporean majority in the APOs, despite the manpower challenges.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: If there is any change to that, it will only be done after a careful review.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Again, our preference would be for there to be more Singaporean APOs.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: But getting Singaporeans with the right qualifications and personality fit has been a challenge for the companies.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Again, because of the overall manpower shortage, of course, you will get someone who will come forward to become an APO but not accepted for the role because the companies do not find him suitable.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: On the deployment of APOs, this depends on the risk assessment and operational requirements of the post.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: We are conscious of the implications of hiring and deploying Malaysian APOs.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Ms Lim also spoke about civilian personnel who are recruited for law enforcement duties and spoke about the gentleman who was deployed by LTA for enforcement duties.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: I think some Government agencies do appoint civilians, including volunteers, as auxiliary officers.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: These agencies will have to have a procedure to recruit, train and audit the officers to ensure that they carry out their duties effectively and professionally.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: There must obviously be a process to pick and train people who are suitable to do the job.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: On the specific case, perhaps if Ms Lim gives me the details, I will ask LTA or check with MOT to see what actually happened.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: I think the fact that someone is 60 should not be a limiting factor, because one can be very fit, and we have to emphasise that.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: So, age of 60 itself should not always be seen as a barrier here.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: But, of course, the personality must be the right fit, and I think, on the specific case, maybe LTA can give an answer.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Ms Lim also asked about the psychological support for prison inmates and the use of their time in prison.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Our prison regime is strict, it is rigorous, with a strong focus on discipline.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: There is no question that it is a no-nonsense environment.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: But the fundamental point is we cannot see prisoners simply as detainees for a period.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: We have to focus on rehabilitation so that, when they leave, they do not go out and re-offend.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: It does not help them, society and the Prison to have them back in the prisons.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Specifically on mental health, the Prison has a multi-disciplinary set of teams, comprising, of course, prison officers, medical officers, psychiatrists, psychologists and counsellors.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: When Prison officers observe inmates exhibiting signs of mental health issues, they will refer them to the psychiatrists and psychologists.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: In addition, members from the Board of Visiting Justices and Board of Visitors conduct regular surprise visits to prison institutions and DRCs to check on inmates' well-being.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Inmates can also approach them during their visits to raise any requests or provide feedback.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: While in prison, the Singapore Prison Service (SPS) has a key focus on rehabilitation.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: The idea is we have to look at it as a continuum, try to do what we can before they offend.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: The Second Minister of Home Affairs Mr Masagos chairs the Committee that looks at that, because we want to try and prevent people from coming into prisons in the first place.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Today, there is data that show what is the likelihood of someone offending from a young age.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: The fact that someone drops out of school is usually an indicator, and there are other indicators.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: You have got to look at this as a continuum and try to treat them in such a way that, first, you reduce the likelihood of them coming into prisons; and, second, when they do come in, you reduce the likelihood of them re-offending.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: So, we take that approach, one picture, not just to look at the period that they are in prison.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: What do we do when they are in prison?

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: They need to, first of all, be taught discipline, some self-control, the ability to control themselves.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Second, once their discipline is established, they should be given training and work programmes – and there are qualifying criteria.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: It depends on how much they might infect the other prisoners, a variety of factors.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: But based on a set of risk assessment tools, prisoners are selected for training, work programmes, so that after they are released, they can get jobs.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Immediately after release is the period when many of them are very vulnerable.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Their old friends approach them, they are ostracised in society and they may not have a job.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: The only people who give them comfort often are not even their families, but their friends who led them astray in the first place.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: So, we have focused quite a bit on what happens post-release.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: It is not perfect, but the hand-holding ‒ the Government, as a partner, bringing in the private sector.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Again, there is a shortage of people that we can use, but we work closely with the private sector to try and get that part going.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: We have been doing this for a number of years and we can do more.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: In terms of the specific questions that have been raised, we enhance their employability through getting them Workforce Skills Qualification training, for example, in numeracy and literacy programmes.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: We have over 12,000 who qualify for training.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: First, we do an assessment on how many qualify.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: In terms of specific drop in numbers, rather than going into specific factors, what I could say is this: the Prison has introduced a programme recently where those who are about to be released, 10 	Page: 72 months pre-release, they will go for intensive counselling.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: That means that they may not be able to go for work programmes.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: That could be one of the reasons why there is a drop in numbers, but there are a number of factors.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: The proportion of qualifying inmates who are engaged in work programmes has actually been increasing.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: There are also religious counselling programmes, family programmes and other counselling programmes to address inmates' drug addiction issues and criminality.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: I do not have the figures for the UK, but if you take Scotland, it is about 40%.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Australia ‒ if we take New South Wales ‒ it is about 48%; Western Australia, 31%; New Zealand, 36%.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: But I do not want to say, therefore, we have reached the best possible state or that it may not go up again, because it is a rate depending on how hardcore these prisoners are.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Parliamentary Secretary Amrin will elaborate on the through-care approach to rehabilitation that SPS adopts.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Mr Perera asked about social impact bonds and whether that can be used to reduce recidivism, almost like the private sector investing in the matter.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: The approach we have taken is to be even more direct by asking the private sector to come in and work with us to employ the people.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: There is a requirement for private sector investment, if I may put it in that way.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: But it is done through, first, identifying while the prisoners are in prison, what are the kinds of job they can do when they come out.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: And then seeing the extent to which we can train them.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Where it is possible to do in-house training, we do it in-house.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Where we need outside consultants to come and help train, we do that, too, so they get trained.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: The statutory board, SCORE, takes care of a number of these things.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: The seriousness with which the Government is approaching this is shown by the fact that we set up a statutory board, which then also works with the private sector, identifies companies which might have an interest in employing these prisoners.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: The Prime Minister launches events relating to the Yellow Ribbon programme, other senior Ministers as well, and keeping it in the public consciousness, and then working with the private sector to try and get them employed.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: As I have said, if I can call it a "scaffolding"; when they are released, you need to try and make sure they move into something.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: If I may say this: seven days a week, 24 hours a day, the work of the Home Team never ceases.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Our officers are on the ground, constantly working to keep Singapore safe and secure.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: Page: 73 You saw this during the Christmas and Chinese New Year periods, especially at the checkpoints.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: More officers were on duty during these peak periods, so that Singaporeans can enjoy the festive seasons.

speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
text: We will press on with our transformation journey, build our capabilities, develop our officers, work closely with the community to meet these challenges head-on and continue to try and keep Singapore safe and secure.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We must adapt and adjust our response to keep pace with developments.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Mr Chris de Souza, Dr Tan Wu Meng and Mr Desmond Choo asked how we will tackle this trend.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Mr de Souza specifically also asked about our capabilities to deal with cybercrime.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: They hide behind the anonymity of the Internet and open and shut down user accounts quickly to evade investigations.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Despite our best efforts and close working relationships with our foreign counterparts, many of these investigations could lead to dead ends.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: So, when it comes to fighting cybercrime, it is especially true that "Prevention is better than cure." An offer that sounds too good to be true may well be a scam.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: People may not be who they claim to be or what their profile pictures on Facebook look like.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We need to be extra careful and alert when performing online transactions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We must watch out not only for ourselves, but also for our children and aged parents and relatives, who may be less aware of these online threats.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: The National Crime Prevention Council has set up a website called Scam Alert which alerts Singaporeans of new scams.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: On Scam Alert, people can share stories about scams that they have come across and you can read about these.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: You will find many similar stories on Scam Alert.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: The victim will usually get an unsolicited message from a young lady on a mobile platform like WeChat.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: In many of these cases, she may be from overseas, has a generic name like "Xiao Yan Zi" and is in Singapore for studies or work.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: She starts chatting to the victim and the conversations sound innocuous at first, but she will soon talk about money problems and how desperate she is for help. "Xiao Yan Zi" will then offer to meet with the victim for sex, $100 or $150 for two hours, more for overnight.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: The victim may reject the offer at first but, after more messages, he agrees to meet "Xiao Yan Zi" somewhere in Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Whether it is for romance or out of curiosity, the victim is already on his way to being scammed.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: And, of course, when he gets to the place, he will not get to meet "Xiao Yan Zi" – she probably is not even in Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Instead, she will ask for the 	Page: 74 victim to pay her first, before coming out to meet him.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: In many of these cases, the request for payment is not by cash, but by purchasing an iTunes card of $100 or $150 and sending over the redemption code by WeChat.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: By the time the victim realises he has been cheated, it is already too late.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: In some stories, the victims get suspicious and call the person on the other end of the line – this is when they discover that "Xiao Yan Zi" sounds much older than she claims to be, or may not even be female.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We have to exercise greater caution and better judgement when we meet strangers or conduct transactions online.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: As all Singaporeans step up our vigilance, Police will also step up their efforts to fight cybercrime.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We will continue to review our laws to address the transnational nature of cybercrime and keep pace with the changing tactics of cyber-criminals.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: (In English): Madam, I will continue in English.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Our approach earlier to cybercrime highlights the need for two important and complementary strategies.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: First, the Home Team will continue our efforts to keep Singapore safe and secure, staying nimble and responsive, upgrading our capabilities and making early investments for the future.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Second, and just as importantly, all Singaporeans have a part to play to be more vigilant and to come together as a community.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: This approach also applies in other domains of safety and security.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: This will be especially important for our border security.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We are trying out some new concepts and technologies for our checkpoints at the new Terminal 4 to prepare ourselves for future challenges.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: These will allow ICA to optimise limited manpower and provide greater border security without compromising service standards.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We plan to roll these initiatives out eventually to all the existing terminals.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Like the Home Team, the private security industry faces a shortage of manpower but ever-growing demand.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: And as Mr Patrick Tay pointed out, technology can be an enabler in the private security industry.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: But mandating the use of technology through law may not be the best approach, given varied security requirements.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Instead, we want to work with private security firms to encourage them to invest in technology.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: First, as a major buyer of security services, the Home Team will restructure our procurement approach to encourage the greater use of technology as part of the security solution.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We are also exploring contracts of longer duration so that the investment in technology can be amortised over a longer period and makes better business sense for our security partners.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: These longer-term contracts will also allow these 	Page: 75 companies to invest in their staff to enhance their productivity.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Second, the Government also provides support to private security agencies through various schemes that are already available to help defray the cost of technology adoption for these companies.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: So, the grant helps security firms adopt technology to boost productivity, but in a way that also benefits the security guards that they employ.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Third, MHA will continue to work with the relevant agencies and industry partners via various platforms, such as the Security Tripartite Cluster, to pilot innovative technology-augmented operating models.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Mr Patrick Tay asked if the building code would be amended to mandate security audits and security threat assessments of commercial buildings and premises.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Building security is critical and we need to do more amidst the current terrorist threat.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: But instead of making it a blanket requirement, we will take a calibrated and differentiated approach.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Today, for sensitive installations and critical infrastructure like Changi Airport, and large building projects with large numbers of visitors, like the Integrated Resorts and Sports Hub, MHA already works with the owners to deploy security measures.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: For soft targets, such as entertainment centres, hotels and shopping centres, we will engage owners through community platforms, such as the Safety and Security Watch Groups (SSWGs), to strengthen security measures.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We will work closely with the owners of these premises and facilities to see how we can implement wider adoption of CCTV coverage that can be used for crime and terrorism prevention and post-incident investigation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: For major events, the Police currently work with organisers to determine the appropriate security measures to be taken.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We will also review our laws to require event organisers to put in place the necessary safety and security measures.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We are mindful of the challenging business environment and potential cost of mandating security measures.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: But we cannot compromise security and expose our public to danger.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: To better manage the costs involved, the Government will work closely with premises owners and event organisers to take cost-effective measures that address our security objectives.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Mr de Souza and Mr Png Eng Huat asked about stateless persons in Singapore and both made speeches earlier about cases that they had encountered.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Mr Png and Mr de Souza asked if we will review the citizenship criteria for such persons who have worked and resided in Singapore for a long time.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: We assess each and every application carefully and compassionately, especially for those who have integrated well and can contribute to Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: But we must be clear-headed about who we grant PR and Singapore citizenship to, and we do not want to automatically grant somebody such a status because he or she has been residing here for a long time.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: But I assure the Members that if they raise cases to our attention, we will look very carefully at the circumstances behind all of them.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Not all the reasons may be apparent to Members but, certainly, we do not reject any case out of hand.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Mr Png also asked about the updating of NRIC details.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: The National Registration Act (NRA) requires NRIC holders to report any change in their place of residence to ICA or the Police within 28 days of the change, regardless of whether an individual is residing at his relative's place temporarily or a rented property.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: The address on the NRIC should be based on the place of physical residence, rather than on ownership of a property.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: This is an individual responsibility and the failure to do so is an offence.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: The Police will act firmly against those who wilfully contravene these requirements to commit other criminal offences, including borrowers who obtain loans from unlicensed money lenders with their outdated addresses.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Mr Png, in a separate cut, suggested tighter controls on where jackpot clubs are sited.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Registered private clubs are permitted to operate jackpot machines only if the machines are provided to their members and guests as part of a whole suite of recreational offerings, which may include karaoke, gyms, swimming pools and so on.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: These machines are not accessible to the general public.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: There are age restrictions barring children from entry and these clubs have to meet other criteria, like the size of their membership base.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Individuals and parents can and should also exercise their own responsibility when using such facilities.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: My Ministry continually reviews our management of "hotspots" with large congregations of foreign workers, such as Little India and Golden Mile.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: This deployment is intensified on weekends and public holidays.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Officers attend training to sensitise them to the culture of foreign workers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Police and relevant agencies also carry out frequent patrols and enforcement checks to deter and detect illegal activities.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: The Special Operations Command conducts a weekly anti-crime patrol to augment Police resources in such "hotspots".

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: The issues extend beyond safety and security concerns and include housing, transport and amenities, amongst other things.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: They host large-scale events like sports competitions, cultural celebrations and movie screenings.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: The Home Team will deal with these firmly, decisively and nimbly to keep Singapore safe and secure.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: I will focus my speech on three areas: first, the community's role in keeping Singapore safe and secure; second, the drug situation in Singapore and our efforts to prevent re-offending; and, third, our Home Team officers and the National Service (NS) Transformation Plan.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: The community is at the heart of the Home Team's work.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Home Team officers take pride and work tirelessly to keep Singapore safe and secure.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: However, the work of the Home Team cannot be accomplished by us alone.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Individuals and the community have contributed in many areas to create a safe and secure Singapore.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: We will continue to engage, empower and partner the community to explore new areas of collaboration.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Over the past few months, as part of the SGfuture engagement efforts, we have asked members of the public, our volunteers, full-time National Servicemen and community partners what safety and security mean to them, what they hope to see and how we may work together to turn these hopes into reality.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: We are now following up on some of these ideas and we welcome more people to come forward with good suggestions that we can work on together.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: One of the key threats we face today is extremism and terrorism.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: The community's role in a heightened terrorism threat environment is critical.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: The programmes under SG Secure will sensitise the community to threats arising from terrorism, extremism and religious or racial strife.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Page: 78 Let me elaborate on how SG Secure will enable the community to "stay alert, stay united and stay strong" against terrorist threats.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: We will raise community vigilance by training the community to be vigilant and alert to unusual behaviour or items in our surroundings and to report these to the authorities.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: We will also teach members of the public how to respond and protect themselves, their family and their friends if they are caught in an attack.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: We need to cherish and safeguard Singapore's multiracial and multi-religious social fabric.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: SG Secure will implement programmes to provide opportunities for our community to appreciate and safeguard racial and religious diversity.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: We will design and run programmes to help our community to be ready to deal with a crisis if it occurs; build individual resilience and community resilience; and help each other bounce back quickly after any incident.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: SG Secure will be more than just a public awareness movement.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Turning to the second part of my speech – the drug situation in Singapore and our efforts to prevent re-offending.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Mr Christopher de Souza and Dr Tan Wu Meng asked about the overall drug situation.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: The drug situation around the world remains challenging.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Poppy cultivation in the region has increased and so has methamphetamine production.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Our regional counterparts have also detected an emergence of overseas syndicates, originating as far as Mexico, which are involved in drug trafficking in the ASEAN region.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: These developments increase the supply of drugs in our region and threaten our drug-free society.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: There is also growing international pressure on our zero-tolerance approach against drugs.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Some countries have pushed to decriminalise or even legalise drug use.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: There is a growing call for the harm reduction approach, which includes measures, such as needle exchange programmes or opiate substitution therapy.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: These measures were implemented in some countries to curb secondary issues, for example, HIV transmission caused by drug abuse.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: However, the harm reduction approach is not relevant in Singapore's context as our drug situation is very much under control.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Incidence of HIV transmission through injecting drug use in Singapore is low.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: We share Mr Christopher de Souza, Dr Tan Wu Meng, Mr Desmond Choo and Mr Gan Thiam Poh's concerns on the local drug abuse situation.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Close to seven in 10 new abusers arrested are below 30 years old.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Second, while methamphetamine remains the most abused drug among new abusers, we have seen more cases of cannabis abuse among new abusers in recent years.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Notably, in 2015, cannabis has displaced heroin as the second most commonly abused drug among new abusers.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Page: 79 These trends indicate that more young people are taking casual attitudes towards drugs and experimenting with drugs, especially cannabis, which they perceive as "soft" and less harmful.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: A research team comprising medical professionals from the Institute of Mental Health (IMH) has reviewed more than 500 papers from respected international medical journals.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Long-term use of cannabis has been linked to the development of major psychiatric conditions, such as schizophrenia, depression and bipolar disorder.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Third, a young person abusing cannabis will experience a persistent and irreversible decline in cognitive development and a drop in IQ.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: To continue keeping Singapore drug-free, we must maintain a zero-tolerance approach towards drug abuse.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: This includes firm law against traffickers, continued enforcement efforts, structured rehabilitation programmes, preventive drug education, as well as aftercare schemes with community support.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Last year, the Task Force on Youths and Drugs reviewed the youth drug abuse situation and announced its recommendations in June.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: The ACE programme is targeted at youth abusers under 21 years old who have abused drugs but tested negative in their urine tests.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: The programme comprises group counselling sessions to equip the youths with skills to cope with addiction and workshop for parents to provide support for youths.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: The Committee Against Youth Drug Abuse, which I chair, will build on the Task Force's work.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: This multi-agency committee comprises representatives from MHA, MOE, HPB, IMH, Institutes of Higher Learning and youths.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: We will continue to keep a close eye on the youth drug abuse situation and work with groups, such as youth groups, to implement initiatives that will sustain efforts in tackling youth drug abuse early.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: I will now touch on our efforts to prevent re-offending, which Mr Louis Ng has asked about.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Our rehabilitation programmes are designed based on evidence to reduce their re-offending.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: We adopt a differentiated approach towards rehabilitation by tailoring the rehabilitation programmes and aftercare support based on the different risk profiles and needs of the offenders.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Page: 80 For example, in the DRCs, drug abusers with more severe drug addiction issues will receive higher intensity programmes, such as more counselling programmes.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: When they are placed on Community-Based Programmes, inmates with higher risk of re-offending would be placed in a more structured environment, such as a halfway house.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: We have also started a day-release arrangement for a small number of low-risk drug abusers.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Under this arrangement, drug abusers are allowed to work or study in the community after two to four months in the DRC.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: These drug abusers are required to return to a community facility at night and are subjected to supervision, such as regular urine tests.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Mr Chairman, Mr Louis Ng, Dr Tan Wu Meng and Mr Patrick Tay asked about the employment of ex-offenders, which is key in their successful reintegration.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: The Singapore Corporation of Rehabilitative Enterprises (SCORE) plays a key role in reintegrating ex-offenders back into the workforce.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: SCORE has also explored new collaboration opportunities with employers and partners.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: For example, SCORE has worked with the Restaurant Association of Singapore (RAS) to develop a Train-Place-Retain model to place ex-offenders in the F&B sector.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: As of February 2016, over 130 ex-offenders secured employment with close to 100 companies from RAS under this collaboration.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: In line with SkillsFuture, SCORE has worked with employers in key sectors, such as Logistics, F&B and Hospitality, to update its skills training and coaching programmes to meet the evolving skills needed.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: For instance, ex-offenders in the F&B sector will be trained in skills required to perform both serving and food preparation functions.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Second, ex-offenders are encouraged to take personal responsibility for their continuous learning with the use of SkillsFuture credits.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Third, SCORE will work closely with employers to identify suitable training for the career advancement of ex-offenders they have hired.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Mr Christopher de Souza asked about the employment of ex-offenders in the Public Service.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: The Public Service recruits on the basis of merit, where applicants who fit most closely to the job requirements are hired.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: When applying for Public Service jobs, applicants who have had their criminal records spent need not include this information in their application.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: As we do not differentiate these employees, ex-offenders will be assessed for their suitability for the job like all other new recruits.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Mr Chairman, with your permission, I will now speak in Malay.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: (In Malay):   The Home Team enjoys a close partnership with the Malay/Muslim community and community groups, such as MENDAKI, MUIS, PERGAS, Jamiyah and Pertapis.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Minister Masagos has built a strong foundation for the Home Team's work with the Malay/Muslim community.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: We will continue to work with the Malay/Muslim community to 	Page: 81 prevent re-offending and rehabilitate drug abusers.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: These are national issues, and not issues involving the Malay/Muslim community only.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: A confluence of factors, such as socio-economic status, peers and families, might play a role in re-offending.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: We have tailored our rehabilitation programmes to address these risk factors.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: We want to work with Malay/Muslim community groups to tailor programmes relevant to the offenders' cultural and religious context to increase their efficacy.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: MENDAKI connects them to community resources, such as counselling at family service centres or employment assistance at the Community Development Centres.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: MENDAKI also refers these families to the family and children programmes they organise.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Through this, we help families stay intact through this difficult period, so that they can support their loved ones in their rehabilitation and reintegration.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: The team at PERGAS, led by Ustaz Mohd Yusri Yubhi Yusoff, developed the programme based on both Islamic teachings and scientific studies that were proven effective.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: This programme is one of the interventions in our multi-pronged approach in rehabilitating drug abusers.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Currently, we are in the midst of a pilot run with inmates in the DRC.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: We are heartened by the encouraging and positive feedback received from those who participated in the programme.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: I recently met Jesyharianti, who was a former drug abuser featured on Suria's Detik programme last month.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: She shared how she had been in and out of prison in the past seven years due to drugs and other offences even though she is only in her 20s.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: During her last incarceration, she was placed on rehabilitation programmes to help her stay drug-free.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Recently, I met Jesy and am happy to know that Jesy is now employed as a service crew with Manhattan Fish Market.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: I also met her employer from Manhattan Fish Market.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: I am heartened to learn that Jesy is one of his best employees.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Jesy's dedication at work often received praises from her customers.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: I hope that the Malay/Muslim community will continue to give the Home Team its fullest support, including in the area of reducing offending and drug abuse.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: (In English):	Mr Chairman, I will continue my speech in English and turn to the final area of my speech.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Our Home Team Officers are a very important part of the Home Team.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Minister Shanmugam spoke about enhancing the attractiveness of the Police career with the Home Team to better recruit and retain officers.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: We will also continue to tap on the contributions of ex-officers, as well as retired officers, which Mr Patrick Tay and Mr Desmond Choo asked about.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Beyond 55 years old, where there are organisational needs, officers may be offered the opportunity to work up to the age of 60, subject to performance, conduct and fitness criteria.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Page: 82 This allows the Home Team to tap on their experience, knowledge and expertise built up over the years.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: We will periodically review the need to make changes to the retirement age of our uniformed officers.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: We will also offer retired officers positions in civilian specialist and civilian roles when they can contribute to the Home Team.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: In addition to retired officers, I agree with Mr Patrick Tay that ex-Police officers are a valuable recruitment pool for SPF.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Suitable ex-Police officers who had resigned may be re-hired, if they wish to rejoin the service.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: SPF proactively reaches out to this group by holding re-appointment exercises twice a year, and SPF will send a personalised letter to invite them to rejoin SPF.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Subsequently, recruitment career advisors, who are Police officers from the same Division, will contact the ex-Police officers to engage them.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Our National Servicemen also play a key role in the Home Team's work.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: However, given the smaller birth cohorts, we can expect a decline in the number of NSFs over the next few years.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: As Mr Melvin Yong has pointed out, we need to ensure that the Home Team continues to meet the growing operational demands even with a declining National Servicemen population.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: The Home Team has embarked on an NS Transformation Plan for our SPF and SCDF National Servicemen.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Over the next few years, we will systematically deploy more NSF and NSmen to frontline positions, leadership roles, as well as specialist positions.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: This will enable them to make stronger contributions to keep Singapore safe and secure.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: ProCom officers will be trained and deployed to protect our critical infrastructure in National Emergency situations and oversee protective security functions during peacetime.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: SCDF has established new NSmen positions in its Marine Command, where NSmen are deployed in daily operations as part of their In-Camp Training.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: SCDF will also deploy more servicemen to operational roles, such as in its Emergency Medical Services.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: I hope that the Transformation Plan will empower our National Servicemen to take on a greater role in making Singapore a safer home for all.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: This is a cumulative effort built over many years and by many people.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: We will continue to strengthen community partnerships, empower our community to take ownership of safety and security issues, and build community vigilance, cohesion and resilience.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: We must also continue our fight against drugs and work hard to prevent offending and re-offending.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs (Mr Amrin Amin)
text: Together, we can keep Singapore safe and secure.

speaker: The Chairman
text: We have a few minutes of clarification time.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
text: First, thank you for walking the ground with us at Little India last month.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
text: Page: 83 My first question is for the Minister to maybe share his thoughts about what he found on the last visit to Little India, if he thought anything needs to change or to be done further.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
text: My second supplementary clarification is on the Ministry's views on what criteria should be used for deciding the locations to allow operators of licences, such as pawnshops, moneylending businesses, sale of alcohol, cyber-game cafes and so forth.

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
text: What are some of the criteria for MHA or Police to decide on where these businesses should be located?

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
text: Should they be located at places, such as void decks and in estates, whether they are public or private housing, because these are actually where residents live day in day out and they are there for the longest time?

speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng
text: And would the Ministry not agree that it is better for places, such as void decks and communal spaces, to have more wholesome community services, such as childcare, SSO or the Senior Activity Centres?

speaker: The Chairman
text: Ms Denise Phua, you are taking a very long time for your question.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: And you will see, generally, where massage establishments are allowed, liquor shops are allowed.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: As for the rest, it is not something that MHA deals with.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: But, of course, some of the regulatory agencies have some supervision.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: If I may go on to talk about Little India.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: We spent, I think, close to three hours, maybe even more.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: And we chose a day when, specifically, it was expected to be crowded, the first Sunday of the month.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: The Police are doing everything they can to deal with the situation.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: But that does not necessarily mean that the entire situation cannot lead to another incident.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: What we are getting in a small area is a very large number of young men.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: We have very strict rules on consumption of liquor and where they can be consumed, but we cannot prevent them from congregating in a variety of places as long as they do not have, say, liquor openly being helped.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: While it is a situation where the best answer I can give you is that I can see that the Police officers, the Auxiliary Police officers, as well as the other uniformed personnel we have put without full Police powers, are doing a very good job.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: But, nevertheless, we cannot put our hand on our heart, given the numbers who are congregating, that something may not happen, and we have to see what else we need to do.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
text: Mr Chairman, my clarification is really on the continuing war on drugs and, in particular, DRC.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
text: The four rationales for sentencing: incarceration − and that is what we do in DRC − we incarcerate the inmates, take them out of the cycle of abuse of drugs where they will not be abusing drugs.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
text: There is the rationale of deterrence: putting them in incarcerated premises to deter them and to deter society from doing something similar like abuse, and there is rehabilitation, in order to rehabilitate the addicts so that the recidivism rate goes down.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
text: I think these three have to be looked at in tandem and worked at in tandem.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
text: Therefore, I appreciate the answers given by the Minister and office bearers.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
text: What more can we do while the addicts are in DRC − which is called the Drug Rehabilitative Centre for a reason − what more can we do when the addicts are there, to really attempt to rehabilitate them?

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
text: We have got them in there for four months, six months.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
text: It is a fertile opportunity for them to help them kick the habit, provided they want to kick the habit.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
text: And my suggestions are counselling, concerted counselling, concerted psychological intervention, vocational training, exercise, so that their memory of the pleasure zones of drugs which they may hark back to is usurped by this new territory of good and wholesome activities.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
text: And also, post-release, what can we do to work with the families and work with their support regimes to, again, distract these former addicts from relapsing, and there is much to be gleaned from this – a lower recidivism rate, which means lower demands for these drugs?

speaker: The Chairman
text: Mr de Souza, I think the Minister gets your point.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
text: So, I ask, what more can be done during the time the addicts are incarcerated for all of these consequential benefits that could be gleaned?

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: The importance of rehabilitation, the importance of reducing recidivism, we all accept that.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: In fact, I said we are even going upstream to see whether we can even prevent offending in the first place.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: And I said, specifically in answer to Ms Lim, we look at them before they come in, try and identify who is at risk during the period to see how we can help them and then post-release.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: And that applies to DRC inmates as well.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: The specific points that Mr de Souza made about counselling, psychological training, those are already being done.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: There is fairly intensive effort made to try and get them to kick the habit.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: First of all, of course, by isolating them from drugs but, second, also trying to get them to understand the dangers of the drug, seeing how they have got into this habit and how they can be helped to kick the habit.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: And post-release, we try a fair bit of intervention but I have to say quite a bit also depends on the family environment and family support.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: We have not received the kind of family participation in programmes that we would like.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: We have programmes that are catered to try and get the kid better but also working with the family.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: But parents often do not come for this.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: So, you see, the state trying to do this by itself is really fighting the problem with one hand tied.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: The more important hand is really the family and we have programmes to bring the family in.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: I have asked my officials to see in what other way we can bring the family in more effectively.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: We have to look at those options and try and see how families can, for example, be directed to come in and help, work with them.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: During the Minister's reply earlier, he did say that work while in prison prepares the inmate, in one sense, for employment post-release.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: But does he also agree that work has some other benefits as it enables the prisoner to come out of the cell and, in many cases, enables him to earn some money, sometimes to send it back to his family, which is very good for self-esteem?

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: Is it because there are insufficient work places available to cater for all who qualify?

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: And, third, I wonder if the Minister is able to share whether he knows how long the average waiting time is for those who are waiting for work.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: On the first point, yes, if they are able to work, obviously, it helps in their self-esteem.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: We would like as many of them as possible to work, provided always that, in the first place, they qualify.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: I have set out some of the criteria, including our assessment of the risks they pose to the prison environment and the possibility of infecting others and how dangerous they are.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Some do not qualify, for example, those on the capital punishment list.

speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan
text: Can I ask the Minister or the Senior Minister of State to give a reply as the topic was not responded to?

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: The Traffic Police (TP) will continue to maintain its enforcement stance against errant drivers.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Mr Lim spoke specifically about sports cars using roads in Mountbatten as a speeding track.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: TP also runs dedicated operations against racing and this new enhanced technology will, hopefully, be of some help.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Anyone caught racing illegally will be severely dealt with.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Mr Lim asked about heavy vehicles, which Mr Tay also mentioned.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: TP also conducts operations against heavy vehicle speeding but enforcement on its own is not sufficient.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: A key strategy is to educate and engage heavy vehicle drivers on road safety and good driving practices.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: So, this year, TP will partner stakeholders, including vehicle inspection centres like VICOM, associations of companies that deploy heavy vehicles and the Workplace Safety and Health Council, to carry out a dedicated outreach campaign for heavy vehicle drivers.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Page: 86 TP will also continue to work with partners like Road Safety Council and Shell Singapore on road safety education for our young or vulnerable road users.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Mr Tay pointed out that besides schools, there are also other places like childcare centres and also enrichment centres where children frequent.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: It may not be practical for us to replicate school zones everywhere because these centres are everywhere.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: But let me assure the Member that we will continue our efforts to keep our roads safe and secure through a whole range of efforts.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Technology has got to come in to a large extent and it has to help us in identifying suspicious patterns.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: I do not want to go into too many operational details but, today, you have the ability to often predict some events happening even before they actually happen based on data that is collected and then analysed through technology.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Then, the human intervention comes in, post that, to try and assess the likelihoods.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Should an incident happen, then you would also want to track.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: They found evidence in dustbins based on cameras which caught their movements.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: You track the entire movement chain from beginning to the end, through a series of cameras.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: You will use it post-incident for investigations, pre-incident for analysis and predictions.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: There is a sort of a framework or a position on that which is in place for the Ministry to do that.

speaker: The Chairman
text: We only have time for one more question.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: Because of such data that can be accessed, I wonder if there are any safeguards so that such access would not be abused.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: The guidelines, the rules, framework, on how the data can be used, can be put in place.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: But you have seen from past incidents, not just from Singapore, in other places as well, there are always possibilities that some individuals may then not use it appropriately.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: That does not, therefore, lead to the conclusion that because there is a possibility of abuse, you do not collect the data or use it in the first place.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Then, you are opening yourself up for an attack which you cannot do anything about and, post-attack, you do not have the tools to investigate.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: In the end, not just this power, a variety of powers that are placed in the hands of the Government, they have to be used within the framework of the law and for the purposes they are given.

speaker: The Chairman
text: Mr de Souza, would you like to withdraw the amendment?

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
text: Before I do so, I would like to place on record that the Home Team is, indeed, really frontline – roads, police coast guard, airport, ambulance and SCDF, ISD.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
text: They provide us with an umbrella of protection, together with MINDEF.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
text: But every day a calamity is avoided is a day of battle won.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
text: Unglamorous because it is a non-event, but hugely important to all of us as Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
text: Before withdrawing this amendment, I say that, also, similarly, Singaporeans need to carry this umbrella together with the Home Team and, should an attack happen in Singapore, respond hand-in-hand with the Home Team to overcome adversity.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
text: With that, I record the House's thanks to the diligent work of the Home Team, its officers, and I beg leave to withdraw my amendment.
